body.statement: Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\), a valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\) is supplied, and fix a successful finite output of \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\). Work on the resulting certificate event, on which \(h_{G,e}\) is nonzero. The real supported source set \(\{(\Lambda,\Omega):\Lambda\in\mathbb R^D,\ \Omega\succ0,\ \Omega_{ij}=0\text{ if }i\leftrightarrow j\notin B\}\) is Euclidean open in its support space and Zariski dense in the complex source space. Since \(\mathcal E_{G,e}\) is proper on the model image, there is a real supported source point \((\Lambda_0,\Omega_0)\) whose covariance \(\Sigma_0\) lies in \(\mathcal M_G\setminus\mathcal E_{G,e}\). A smooth semialgebraic stratification refined by the real-lifting sign conditions contains \(\Sigma_0\) in a connected cell \(\mathcal C_{G,e}\) on which real-extension status is constant, and a sufficiently small closed chart ball gives a nonempty compact \(\mathcal K_G\subset\mathcal C_{G,e}\) with nonempty relative interior. For every \(\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G\), \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\ne\varnothing\), because membership in \(\mathcal M_G\) supplies at least one complete real supported \(\Lambda\).
body.proof_tex:
Work under the valid-chart and successful-output antecedents.  On this event, \(\mathrm{thm:exceptional\mbox{-}set\mbox{-}validity}\) says that \(h_{G,e}\) is nonzero in the covariance-model coordinate ring.  Put
\[
 N=|D|+|B|+n
\]
and identify the free real entries of \((\Lambda,\Omega)\), subject only to the prescribed support, with \(\mathbb R^N\).  The set
\[
 \mathcal S_+
 =\{(\Lambda,\Omega)\in\mathbb R^N:\Omega\succ0\}           \tag{22}
\]
is nonempty because it contains \((0,I_n)\), and is Euclidean open in this support space because strict positive definiteness is stable under sufficiently small perturbations.

The set \(\mathcal S_+\) is Zariski dense in the corresponding complex source space.  Indeed, it contains a real open box about \((0,I_n)\).  If a complex polynomial vanishes on that box, fix all but one coordinate; the resulting univariate polynomial has infinitely many roots and is zero.  Repeating this argument coordinate by coordinate makes every coefficient zero.

For the fixed acyclic graph, define the source parametrization
\[
 \Phi_G(\Lambda,\Omega)
 =(I_n-\Lambda)^{-\mathsf T}\Omega(I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}.         \tag{23}
\]
In a topological order \(\Lambda^n=0\), so each inverse in (23) is the finite sum \(I_n+\Lambda+\cdots+\Lambda^{n-1}\); hence \(\Phi_G\) is polynomial.  Nonzeroness of \(h_{G,e}\) in \(R_G\) means that the source polynomial \(h_{G,e}\circ\Phi_G\) is nonzero.  Zariski density of (22) therefore supplies \((\Lambda_0,\Omega_0)\in\mathcal S_+\) such that
\[
 h_{G,e}(\Phi_G(\Lambda_0,\Omega_0))\ne0.                    \tag{24}
\]
With \(\Sigma_0=\Phi_G(\Lambda_0,\Omega_0)\), equation (24) gives
\[
 \Sigma_0\in\mathcal M_G\setminus\mathcal E_{G,e}.          \tag{25}
\]

The model image is semialgebraic: it is the projection of the source set described by the polynomial covariance equations, the linear missing-bidirected equalities, and the strict principal-minor inequalities for \(\Omega\succ0\); effective real quantifier elimination removes the source coordinates.  The exceptional complement and each sign condition in the real-lifting formula are semialgebraic as well.  Outside the leading-coefficient and squarefreeness factors in \(h_{G,e}\), the degree of \(p_e(\Sigma,\cdot)\) is fixed and every root is simple.  The assertion that \(z\) is the \(j\)-th real root is an ordered-field formula: it asserts \(p_e(\Sigma,z)=0\) and the existence of exactly \(j-1\) distinct real roots below \(z\).  Clearing the certified nonzero denominators and applying quantifier elimination shows that each ordered-root graph is semialgebraic.  Intersecting it with the real-lifting sign formula and projecting to covariance space shows that the locus on which that ordered root is extendable is also semialgebraic.

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:semialgebraic\mbox{-}stratification}\) to the finite common refinement by the model image, the exceptional complement, the possible real-root counts, and these extendability loci, and split the resulting smooth strata into connected components.  The component through \(\Sigma_0\) is a connected smooth semialgebraic cell
\[
 \mathcal C_{G,e}\subseteq
 \mathcal M_G\setminus\mathcal E_{G,e}                       \tag{26}
\]
on which the number of simple real roots and every ordered root's extension label are constant.  This is the cell required by \(\mathrm{def:regular\mbox{-}cell}\).

Choose a smooth coordinate chart \(u:U\to u(U)\subseteq\mathbb R^s\) of this cell about \(\Sigma_0\).  If \(s>0\), choose \(\rho>0\) with \(\overline B(u(\Sigma_0),\rho)\subset u(U)\), and define
\[
 \mathcal K_G
 =u^{-1}\!\left(\overline B(u(\Sigma_0),\rho)\right).        \tag{27}
\]
If \(s=0\), set \(\mathcal K_G=\{\Sigma_0\}\).  In both cases \(\mathcal K_G\) is nonempty and compact and has nonempty relative interior in \(\mathcal C_{G,e}\), as required by \(\mathrm{def:regular\mbox{-}class}\).

Finally, fix \(\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G\).  Since \(\Sigma\in\mathcal M_G\), its definition supplies real supported \(\Lambda\) and \(\Omega\succ0\) satisfying (23).  Multiplying by \((I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\) and \(I_n-\Lambda\) gives
\[
 \Omega=(I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_n-\Lambda).       \tag{28}
\]
For every missing bidirected pair, expansion of (28) gives \(F_{ij}(\Lambda,\Sigma)=\Omega_{ij}=0\).  Hence the real value \(\lambda_e\) has a complete real supported extension, and by definition
\[
 \lambda_e\in\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma).                         \tag{29}
\]
Thus \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\ne\varnothing\) throughout \(\mathcal K_G\).
body.justification: The regular statistical domain must be shown nonvacuous and its real identified set must be nonempty rather than imposed by assumption.
body.gap: Standard stratification arguments isolate smooth cells, but the stated lemma ties such a cell to the certified SEM exceptional locus and to rootwise real extension.
body.consumer: The inference theorem obtains a genuine compact operating region and a nonempty target set on every data-generating covariance in that region.
